title: Request Exit Signal Canvas and SLO-aware Remediation Dashboards
creator: Devon Chen
description: Goal: Build a single-pane 'Exit Signal Canvas' that enumerates request termination modes across the inference stack (network/gateway, transport, runtime queueing, GPU execution, model-level terminations) and power dashboards + drilldowns that map those signals to SLO exposure and remediation guidance. Background: We have many dashboards surfacing errors and latency islands but lack a canonical mapping from the raw exit modes emitted by runtime/gateway/traces to operator actions. This ticket scopes the taxonomy, schema changes for trace hooks, metric/log ingestion updates, dashboard wireframes, and a phased rollout plan with canary sampling. Scope: 1) Define canonical exit_code enums and human-readable categories (e.g., client-cancel, network-abort, http-5xx, grpc-status-13-DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, cpu-oom, gpu-out-of-memory, kvcache-miss-eviction, model-internal-error, model-rejection, rate-limited, overloaded-queue-drop). 2) Add structured trace attributes: trace.exit.code, trace.exit.stage, trace.exit.reason, trace.rollout.fallback_model. 3) Emit aggregate metrics (counter and histograms) and structured log lines to existing metrics/log pipelines. 4) Dashboard deliverables: overview distribution, per-route per-model heatmaps, time-series SLO exposure (p99/p95 error-burden), cohort drilldown for retry/fallback effectiveness. 5) Playbook snippets for common signals (timeout vs overload vs model-error) with suggested mitigation (route to cheaper model variant, increase burst capacity, tune batcher, adjust retry/backoff). Success metrics: Exit signal coverage >= 95% of observed terminations in staging; dashboards show SLO exposure and actionable remediation; oncall runbook updated. Non-goals: Automated routing changes (separate infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical exit_code enum and README published to Confluence with mappings to raw runtime/gateway signals
Trace schema updates landed (trace.exit.* attributes) and instrumented in runtime with unit tests
Metrics and structured logs emitted for every termination path in staging and consumed by dashboards
Dashboards implemented: Exit Signal Overview, Per-model Exit Distribution, SLO Exposure timeline, and Drilldown for retries/fallbacks
Playbook with 6 common remediation entries added to runbook; oncall walkthrough completed

technical_notes: Trace attribute schema: trace.exit.code (string), trace.exit.stage (one of: gateway, transport, queue, runtime, model), trace.exit.reason (freeform), trace.rollout.fallback_model (string)
Metric plan: counter(exit_code) with tags [route, model, region, node_pool]; histogram(request.latency_ms) with exit_code tag to calculate p95/p99 per-exit mode
Log lines should include structured 'exit' block to enable ELK/Kafka parsers; use existing schema version v2 for compatibility

Dashboard calculation: SLO exposure = sum(tokens_lost * cost_per_token) for requests with exit_code in [http-5xx, grpc-13, model-error] binned by minute; highlight bursts where exposure > 5% of SLO budget
Sampling: start with full traces for failed requests, 2% sampling for successful requests in canary clusters. Add toggles to tracing agent to reduce cardinality of unusual exit reasons.
risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality exit reasons from model internals could explode metrics. Mitigation: normalize freeform reasons into buckets during ingestion and cap cardinality at source.
Duplicated termination events (runtime + autoscaler) may double-count. Mitigation: add dedupe key combining request_id and stage before incrementing counters (ENG-922000).
Regression risk when adding trace attributes to runtime. Mitigation: feature flag and staged rollout, tests asserting no serialization regressions.
notes: Design trade-off: using a single string field for transport codes simplifies dashboards but requires parsing logic in queries; chosen for easier backwards compatibility.
We intentionally exclude automated routing changes from this ticket to keep scope focused on observability and operator UX.
Next steps: finalize enum, land runtime PR, set up ingestion pipeline transforms, and ship dashboards to staging for 24h observation window.
